articles.title: How Israel's E1 plan in West Bank threatens a future Palestinian state
articles.titleCn: 以色列在约旦河西岸的E1计划如何威胁未来的巴勒斯坦国

The European response reflects growing concern that continued settlement expansion could make a negotiated two-state solution increasingly difficult to implement. Cui Hongjian, a professor at Beijing Foreign Studies University's Academy of Regional and Global Governance, said the EU wants to prevent further {{19}} of Israel's actions in the West Bank, which could {{20}} the conflict involving Israel, Iran and the United States and put European interests more directly at risk. On August 21, the foreign ministers of Egypt, Jordan, the UAE, Indonesia, Pakistan, Türkiye, Saudi Arabia and Qatar also condemned the E1 plan. The European and Middle Eastern reactions both reflect the same concern: continued settlement expansion could create {{21}} "facts on the ground," undermine prospects for a Palestinian state and further {{22}} conflict in the region.

paragraphs.en:
Israel's expanding settlements and settler violence
The West Bank was {{23}} by Israel in the 1967 war and has remained under Israeli control since then. Under international law, Israel is {{24}} from establishing settlements in the territory it occupies. The BBC reported that Israel has built about 160 settlements housing some 700,000 Israelis in the West Bank since 1967. E1 is part of a broader expansion of Israeli settlements across the West Bank. The expansion has been accompanied by growing settler violence against Palestinians.
paragraphs.cn: 以色列不断扩张的定居点和定居者暴力。约旦河西岸在1967年战争中被以色列占领，此后一直处于以色列控制之下。根据国际法，以色列被禁止在其占领的领土上建立定居点。BBC报道称，自1967年以来，以色列已在约旦河西岸建造了约160个定居点，容纳约70万以色列人。E1是以色列在约旦河西岸更广泛扩张的一部分。这种扩张伴随着针对巴勒斯坦人的定居者暴力日益增多。

paragraphs.en:
Most recently, in August, Israeli settlers {{26}} three Palestinian homes in the West Bank village of Qusra for several days, cutting off water and electricity and preventing residents from leaving. US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee, a longtime supporter of Israeli settlements, also condemned the attackers as "terrorists."
UN figures show the scale of the violence. Since the beginning of 2026, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) had documented more than 1,380 settler-related incidents have been documented, affecting over 250 Palestinian communities and averaging about 6.6 incidents per day. During the same period, around 900 Palestinians had been injured in settler attacks, while more than 2,300 had been {{27}} by settler attacks and related access restrictions. OCHA also reported that 76 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli forces or settlers or died of wounds sustained earlier since the beginning of 2026.
paragraphs.cn: 最近，8月份，以色列定居者包围了约旦河西岸库斯拉村的三户巴勒斯坦民居数日，切断水电，阻止居民离开。长期支持以色列定居点的美国驻以色列大使迈克·赫卡比也谴责袭击者为"恐怖分子"。联合国数据显示了暴力的规模。自2026年初以来，联合国人道主义事务协调厅已记录了超过1380起与定居者相关的事件，影响了250多个巴勒斯坦社区，平均每天约6.6起。同期，约有900名巴勒斯坦人在定居者袭击中受伤，而超过2300人因定居者袭击和相关通行限制而流离失所。人道协调厅还报告称，自2026年初以来，已有76名巴勒斯坦人被以色列军队或定居者杀害，或因先前受伤而死亡。

paragraphs.en: The violence has involved physical assaults as well as attacks on homes, farmland, water systems and other {{28}} infrastructure. Against this backdrop, the E1 project goes beyond the construction of new homes. Settlement expansion, infrastructure development, restrictions on Palestinian communities and settler violence are changing the geography of the West Bank, making a geographically {{29}} Palestinian state increasingly difficult.
paragraphs.cn: 暴力涉及人身攻击以及针对房屋、农田、供水系统和其他生计基础设施的袭击。在此背景下，E1项目不仅仅是建造新住房。定居点扩张、基础设施开发、对巴勒斯坦社区的限制和定居者暴力正在改变约旦河西岸的地理格局，使地理上可行的巴勒斯坦国变得越来越困难。

articles.fullText:
An Israeli security checkpoint checks car entering Jerusalem from the E1 area, where the Israeli government plans to build housing units, in the eastern edge of the Judean Desert, West Bank, on Thursday, August 20, 2026. 
Israel's plan to build new settlements in the E1 area of the occupied West Bank has drawn widespread international condemnation, with the international community warning that the project could further undermine the territorial continuity needed for a future Palestinian state.
E1 covers about 12 square kilometers between East Jerusalem and the settlement of Maale Adumim, one of the largest Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. Israel has planned to build settlements there since the 1990s, but the project has repeatedly been delayed amid international pressure.
On August 18, Israeli authorities opened a tender for 1,234 of the 3,401 housing units approved by the Israeli government last August.
The significance of E1 lies in its location. The area connects East Jerusalem with Maale Adumim. Building settlements there would link existing Israeli settlements, further fragmenting the West Bank and severing the territorial connection between East Jerusalem and other Palestinian areas.
This is why the project is widely seen as a threat to the two-state solution. Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas said it would undermine prospects for an independent Palestinian state based on the 1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital.
Abbas said the E1 plan violates international law and UN Security Council Resolution 2334. Adopted in 2016, the resolution calls on Israel to "immediately and completely cease all settlement activities" in the occupied Palestinian territory, including East Jerusalem.
East Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza Strip form a geographic and political entity and constitute the occupied Palestinian territory, Abbas said, adding that settlement expansion and annexation cannot create legal rights or change the territory's legal status.
Why has the plan triggered international condemnation?
The plan has triggered strong international condemnation, particularly from Europe and the Middle East.
On August 20, Britain, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway and Canada condemned the E1 tender as "unacceptable," saying it would fragment the West Bank, damage Palestinian territorial continuity and undermine the prospects of a two-state solution.
The European response reflects growing concern that continued settlement expansion could make a negotiated two-state solution increasingly difficult to implement.
Cui Hongjian, a professor at Beijing Foreign Studies University's Academy of Regional and Global Governance, said the EU wants to prevent further escalation of Israel's actions in the West Bank, which could widen the conflict involving Israel, Iran and the United States and put European interests more directly at risk.
On August 21, the foreign ministers of Egypt, Jordan, the UAE, Indonesia, Pakistan, Türkiye, Saudi Arabia and Qatar also condemned the E1 plan.
The European and Middle Eastern reactions both reflect the same concern: continued settlement expansion could create permanent "facts on the ground," undermine prospects for a Palestinian state and further fuel conflict in the region.
Israel's expanding settlements and settler violence
The West Bank was captured by Israel in the 1967 war and has remained under Israeli control since then. Under international law, Israel is prohibited from establishing settlements in the territory it occupies. The BBC reported that Israel has built about 160 settlements housing some 700,000 Israelis in the West Bank since 1967.
E1 is part of a broader expansion of Israeli settlements across the West Bank.
The expansion has been accompanied by growing settler violence against Palestinians. Most recently, in August, Israeli settlers besieged three Palestinian homes in the West Bank village of Qusra for several days, cutting off water and electricity and preventing residents from leaving. US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee, a longtime supporter of Israeli settlements, also condemned the attackers as "terrorists."
UN figures show the scale of the violence. Since the beginning of 2026, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) had documented more than 1,380 settler-related incidents have been documented, affecting over 250 Palestinian communities and averaging about 6.6 incidents per day.
During the same period, around 900 Palestinians had been injured in settler attacks, while more than 2,300 had been displaced by settler attacks and related access restrictions.
OCHA also reported that 76 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli forces or settlers or died of wounds sustained earlier since the beginning of 2026.
The violence has involved physical assaults as well as attacks on homes, farmland, water systems and other livelihood infrastructure.
Against this backdrop, the E1 project goes beyond the construction of new homes. Settlement expansion, infrastructure development, restrictions on Palestinian communities and settler violence are changing the geography of the West Bank, making a geographically viable Palestinian state increasingly difficult.

articles.title: English hospitals aim to ramp up use of robotics in surgery
articles.titleCn: 英国医院旨在加大手术中机器人技术的应用
articles.summary: The UK government has announced plans to invest more in robotic equipment for English hospitals and set a target for robotic assistance to be used in 90% of keyhole surgeries carried out in England by 2035
articles.summaryCn: 英国政府计划增加对机器人手术设备的投资，目标到2035年90%的微创手术使用机器人辅助，以提升手术精准度并缓解医疗系统压力。

paragraphs.en:
The UK government has announced plans to invest more in {{1}} equipment for English hospitals and set a target for robotic assistance to be used in 90% of {{2}} surgeries carried out in England by 2035. The government highlighted robotics as one of five "big bets" in a 10-year health plan for England, alongside other {{3}} technologies: data, AI, {{4}} and wearables. Surgeons and nurses using the new Da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system while performing surgery, at St Bartholomew's Hospital in London. /Carlos Jasso/AFP
At St Bartholomew's Hospital in central London, visiting surgeons are among the first to be trained to use the new da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system, made by US company Initiative. The system, which includes three robotic arms that can hold surgical equipment, is controlled using an {{5}} 3D headset and a video-game-like {{6}}.
paragraphs.cn: 英国政府宣布计划增加对英格兰医院机器人设备的投资，并设定目标，到2035年，英格兰90%的微创手术将使用机器人辅助。政府将机器人技术列为英格兰十年健康计划中的五大“重大赌注”之一，其他变革性技术包括数据、人工智能、基因组学和可穿戴设备。在伦敦圣巴塞洛缪医院，外科医生和护士正在使用新的达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统进行手术。/Carlos Jasso/AFP

paragraphs.en:
Robotic surgical systems like this can be used across a range of {{7}} including urology, gynecology, abdominal, colorectal, and thoracic or general surgery. Sasha Stamenkovic (C) using the new Da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system while performing lung cancer surgery as Ali Ansaripour (R), senior cardiothoracic trainee on a robotic fellowship, looks on. /Carlos Jasso/AFP
The {{8}} of robotic-assisted surgery should mean shorter hospital stays and quicker recovery times, which will take {{9}} off a struggling health service with year-long waitlists, workforce shortages and discharge {{10}}. "The ability to have lots of {{11}} computer-aided technology on top" of human-controlled robotics "makes this precise surgery. It makes it safe surgery," says Sasha Stamenkovic, Director of Robotic Surgery and Research at Barts Health NHS Trust.
paragraphs.cn: 在伦敦市中心的圣巴塞洛缪医院，来访的外科医生是最早接受使用美国公司Initiative制造的新型达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统培训的人之一。该系统包括三个可持手术器械的机械臂，通过沉浸式3D头显和类似视频游戏的控制台进行操作。

paragraphs.en:
As well as improving recovery times, the greater precision also reduces the risk of {{12}} like air leaks, a common cause of longer hospital stays following lung surgery. Nurses assisting in lung cancer surgery using the new Da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system, at St Bartholomew's Hospital. /Carlos Jasso/AFP
Ian Macleod was the first patient in Britain's NHS to {{13}} lung cancer surgery using the new da Vinci robotic system. Macleod says he "didn't realize" until he was wearing a surgical gown and anesthetised that he would hold this {{14}} title, but the news "didn't {{15}}" the 76-year-old retired detective. Thirty minutes after the robotic-assisted operation, Macleod was back on his feet.
paragraphs.cn: 这类机器人手术系统可用于多种专科，包括泌尿科、妇科、腹部、结直肠、胸外科或普外科。Sasha Stamenkovic（中）使用新的达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统进行肺癌手术，Ali Ansaripour（右）是机器人专科的高级心胸外科培训生，正在观摩。/Carlos Jasso/AFP

paragraphs.en: "It was {{16}}," he says. "In fact, after the operation, I found out quite quickly that I only had one stitch." He had undergone non-robotic keyhole surgery for a different cancer in the past, and says the recovery time was "much longer". articles.fullText:
The UK government has announced plans to invest more in robotic equipment for English hospitals and set a target for robotic assistance to be used in 90% of keyhole surgeries carried out in England by 2035.
The government highlighted robotics as one of five "big bets" in a 10-year health plan for England, alongside other transformative technologies: data, AI, genomics and wearables.
Surgeons and nurses using the new Da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system while performing surgery, at St Bartholomew's Hospital in London. /Carlos Jasso/AFP
At St Bartholomew's Hospital in central London, visiting surgeons are among the first to be trained to use the new da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system, made by US company Initiative. The system, which includes three robotic arms that can hold surgical equipment, is controlled using an immersive 3D headset and a video-game-like console.
Robotic surgical systems like this can be used across a range of specialties including urology, gynecology, abdominal, colorectal, and thoracic or general surgery.
Sasha Stamenkovic (C) using the new Da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system while performing lung cancer surgery as Ali Ansaripour (R), senior cardiothoracic trainee on a robotic fellowship, looks on. /Carlos Jasso/AFP
The precision of robotic-assisted surgery should mean shorter hospital stays and quicker recovery times, which will take strain off a struggling health service with year-long waitlists, workforce shortages and discharge bottlenecks.
"The ability to have lots of integrated computer-aided technology on top" of human-controlled robotics "makes this precise surgery. It makes it safe surgery," says Sasha Stamenkovic, Director of Robotic Surgery and Research at Barts Health NHS Trust.
As well as improving recovery times, the greater precision also reduces the risk of complications like air leaks, a common cause of longer hospital stays following lung surgery.
Nurses assisting in lung cancer surgery using the new Da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system, at St Bartholomew's Hospital. /Carlos Jasso/AFP
Ian Macleod was the first patient in Britain's NHS to undergo lung cancer surgery using the new da Vinci robotic system. Macleod says he "didn't realize" until he was wearing a surgical gown and anesthetised that he would hold this groundbreaking title, but the news "didn't faze" the 76-year-old retired detective.
Thirty minutes after the robotic-assisted operation, Macleod was back on his feet. "It was extraordinary," he says. "In fact, after the operation, I found out quite quickly that I only had one stitch." He had undergone non-robotic keyhole surgery for a different cancer in the past, and says the recovery time was "much longer". This time, he was driving his wife to the garden centrer for coffee less than a week later.
Stamenkovic runs fellowships at St Bartholomew's training surgeons on this new technology. He says it is the young surgeons who pick up the new robotic control system the fastest and who become the most adept.
"They've come with different skill sets," he says, "they've probably come with gaming skill sets, some of them have come with a musical background."
Laying out his long-term mission, Stamenkovic added: "All we need to do is harness their energy, their passion, their skill set, and teach them the right moves. And that will make the surgeon of the future."

英国政府宣布计划增加对英格兰医院机器人设备的投资，并设定目标，到2035年，英格兰90%的微创手术将使用机器人辅助。政府将机器人技术列为英格兰十年健康计划中的五大“重大赌注”之一，其他变革性技术包括数据、人工智能、基因组学和可穿戴设备。在伦敦圣巴塞洛缪医院，外科医生和护士正在使用新的达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统进行手术。/Carlos Jasso/AFP

在伦敦市中心的圣巴塞洛缪医院，来访的外科医生是最早接受使用美国公司Initiative制造的新型达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统培训的人之一。该系统包括三个可持手术器械的机械臂，通过沉浸式3D头显和类似视频游戏的控制台进行操作。

这类机器人手术系统可用于多种专科，包括泌尿科、妇科、腹部、结直肠、胸外科或普外科。Sasha Stamenkovic（中）使用新的达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统进行肺癌手术，Ali Ansaripour（右）是机器人专科的高级心胸外科培训生，正在观摩。/Carlos Jasso/AFP

机器人辅助手术的精准性应能缩短住院时间并加快恢复，从而减轻医疗服务的压力，该系统目前面临长达一年的候诊名单、劳动力短缺和出院瓶颈。“在人类控制的机器人技术之上，集成大量计算机辅助技术的能力，使这种手术精准且安全，”巴茨健康NHS信托的机器人手术与研究主任Sasha Stamenkovic说。

除了改善恢复时间，更高的精准度还降低了并发症风险，如肺手术后常见导致住院时间延长的漏气。在圣巴塞洛缪医院，护士正在协助使用新的达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统进行肺癌手术。/Carlos Jasso/AFP

Ian Macleod是英国NHS中第一位使用新型达芬奇机器人系统进行肺癌手术的患者。Macleod说，直到他穿上手术服并被麻醉时，他才意识到自己将获得这一开创性的称号，但这一消息“没有吓到”这位76岁的退休侦探。机器人辅助手术后三十分钟，Macleod就能重新站起来了。

“这太不可思议了，”他说。“事实上，手术后我很快发现我只有一针缝合。”他过去曾因另一种癌症接受过非机器人微创手术，并表示恢复时间“长得多”。这次，不到一周后，他就开车带妻子去花园中心喝咖啡了。Stamenkovic在圣巴塞洛缪医院运营奖学金项目，培训外科医生使用这项新技术。他说，年轻外科医生掌握新机器人控制系统最快，也最熟练。

“他们带来了不同的技能组合，”他说，“他们可能带来了游戏技能，有些人有音乐背景。”

在阐述他的长期使命时，Stamenkovic补充道：“我们只需要利用他们的能量、热情和技能，教他们正确的动作。这将造就未来的外科医生。”

articles.fullText:
Europe is experiencing a summer of extreme heat and drought, with record temperatures, wildfire risks and falling river levels affecting several countries.
A scorched landscape in the wake of a wildfire that swept through the Gironde region in Lege-Cap-Ferret, southwestern France, August 4, 2026. 
France recorded its hottest July since nationwide records began in 1900, with a monthly average temperature of 24.9 degrees Celsius, according to Meteo-France.
Rainfall across the country was nearly 70% below the seasonal average, making July 2026 the third-driest July on record.
Persistent heat, drought and windy conditions kept wildfire risks high or very high, while a wildfire in the southwestern department of Gironde burned about 42,000 hectares and forced the evacuation of more than 220,000 people.
Boats lie in the dried out riverbed of a branch of the river Danube in Hainburg, Austria, August 3, 2026. 
In Austria, a national temperature record of 41 degrees Celsius was set on Tuesday as the heat wave continued. The record was measured in the Stammersdorf region of Vienna, according to Austria's state broadcaster ORF.
A forest fire is also raging in Burgenland, while the Lobau wetlands in Vienna face the highest fire danger level. Meanwhile, water levels on the Danube River have fallen to historically low levels, comparable to the major low-water years of 2003 and 2018.
The dried-up Danube riverbed with the Paks power plant at the background, near Dunaszentbenedek, close to Paks town, Hungary, July 31, 2026. 
Neighboring Hungary has extended its highest-level heat alert until midnight on Friday as forecasts show the heat wave will continue. Authorities warned that persistent high temperatures could affect everyone and urged people to take precautions.
The heat wave has intensified drought conditions, lowered water levels in major rivers and increased wildfire risks, with firefighters recently responding to around 100 outdoor fires per day.
A firefighting helicopter flies toward a wildfire on a mountain near L'Aquila, central Italy, August 3, 2026. 
Italy is also facing its fourth major heat wave of the summer, with temperatures exceeding 40 degrees Celsius in some areas.
The Health Ministry placed 25 of the country's 27 monitored cities under the highest heat alert, including Rome, Milan, Florence, Bologna, Venice, Naples and Palermo.
Hot and dry conditions have increased wildfire risks and put pressure on agriculture, with farmers reporting reduced crop yields and higher irrigation demand.
A general view of the Paks nuclear power plant, Hungary, July 31, 2026. 
Low river levels and rising water temperatures have also affected nuclear power operations in parts of Europe.
Hungary's Paks nuclear power plant, which supplies nearly half of the country's electricity, remained operational but its operation depended on river conditions and cooling system performance.
Romania's Cernavoda nuclear power plant shut down both reactors after low Danube water levels affected operations. In France and Switzerland, some nuclear facilities also faced operational disruptions as high river temperatures affected cooling capacity.
The combination of extreme heat, drought and declining water availability is putting pressure on public health, agriculture, wildfire prevention and energy systems in affected areas.

articles.fullText:
In Ulan Bator, capital of Mongolia, the 17th session of the Conference of the Parties (COP17) to the UN Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) is underway, with China offering strong support for the summit. Beyond the conference halls, China has long been helping its neighbor tackle a growing threat.
Gorkhi-Terelj National Park, Mongolia. 
More than 70% of Mongolia's territory is affected by desertification, with the southern Gobi region hardest hit. Spring dust storms regularly sweep across the border, making it a shared environmental challenge.
Since signing the UNCCD in 1994, China has evolved from a recipient of international green aid into a global provider of land restoration expertise, becoming the first country to reverse land degradation and shrink its desert footprint. Mongolia is a key partner in this work.
Mongolia faces a critical shortage of sapling nurseries. China has stepped in to fill the gap. North China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region has become Mongolia's primary sapling supplier, shipping over 11.7 million saplings by early June.
Beyond saplings, Inner Mongolian specialists are helping build ecological restoration zones, roll out afforestation models, and launch joint sandstorm monitoring systems, says Hou Shuxia from Inner Mongolia University of Finance and Economics.
The renowned Kubuqi Model, a public-private-people partnership, sits at the heart of this shared toolkit.
Meteorological collaboration is also deepening. In April, the two countries held their first joint video briefing to assess spring dust risks, vegetation growth, and seasonal climate trends. At the 2025 World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai, China donated its AI-powered meteorological warning system MAZU to Mongolia.
A formal anchor came in September 2023, when the China-Mongolia Desertification Prevention and Control Cooperation Center was inaugurated, run by Beijing Forestry University.
Chinese companies are also contributing. In 2022, Shini Shini Co., Ltd., a mining company run by China Railway Resources Group in Dornod Province, launched Mongolia's first waste-free underground backfilling mining system.
By the end of 2025, crews had planted more than 12,000 trees, and reclaimed over 30 hectares of land. The restoration work aligns with Mongolia's 2021 initiative to plant 1 billion trees by 2030.
"We firmly believe mines can serve as models of green development," said Gong Mingshan, executive director of the company.
"We aim to build this mine into a flagship example of China-Mongolia anti-desertification collaboration. We will ramp up environmental investment, advance digital ecological monitoring and low-carbon mining technology, and deepen experience exchanges with Mongolian counterparts," Gong said.

articles.fullText:
Google's head of AI, Demis Hassabis, will step down from his current role to become Alphabet's chief scientist amid a reshuffling at DeepMind that will also include a key engineer's departure.
Hassabis will take on two new titles, Alphabet announced on Wednesday: chair of DeepMind and chief scientist of Alphabet.
The change "will allow me to focus on long-term strategy, and accelerating scientific breakthroughs, including leaning into my work at Isomorphic to help cure disease," Hassabis wrote in a social media post.
Isomorphic Labs is an AI-powered drug discovery lab that spun out from DeepMind in 2021. In 2024, Hassabis won a Nobel Prize in chemistry.
As part of the shake up, DeepMind's chief technology officer and chief AI architect Koray Kavukcuoglu will become the division's senior vice president and oversee its operations, including the development of Google's flagship frontier models and products which are known as Gemini.
Longtime Google engineer Jeff Dean is also leaving the company after nearly three decades to "try something new, and we're excited to support him in that," Google CEO Sundar Pichai said in a blog post announcing the news.
Hassabis co-founded DeepMind in 2010, and four years later, Google bought the research lab for $650 million, according to reports at the time. His co-founder, Mustafa Suleyman, is currently the chief of Microsoft's AI segment.
Google is competing for customers alongside other major AI developers including Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta, as well as DeepSeek and Moonshot in China.
The industry is also chasing a theoretical milestone known as advanced general intelligence (AGI), which is a point when AI software matches the capabilities of human thinking.
"I've been working towards AGI my whole life and now, like many of you, I feel it is close at hand," Hassabis wrote in Wednesday's blog post.
"With this backdrop, I've decided that now is the right time for me to hand over my day-to-day operational responsibilities at (Google DeepMind), so that I have the time and space to focus on the big picture and help influence what is to come," Hassabis continued.
Observers have been waiting for Google to announce a more powerful version of its AI model, called Gemini 3.5 Pro, which was supposed to launch in June but appears to be delayed.
Its shares closed 4% down Wednesday afternoon.
The leadership changes come amid a wider brain drain at Google.
In June, a top AI and engineering executive, Noam Shazeer, left for OpenAI, while senior researcher John Jumper, who shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in chemistry with Hassabis, jumped to Anthropic.

作为重组的一部分，DeepMind的首席技术官兼首席AI架构师科拉伊·卡武克丘奥卢将成为该部门的高级副总裁，并负责其运营，包括开发谷歌旗舰前沿模型和产品，即Gemini。谷歌长期工程师杰夫·迪恩在近三十年后也将离开公司，以“尝试新事物，我们很高兴支持他这样做，”谷歌CEO桑达尔·皮查伊在宣布这一消息的博客文章中表示。哈萨比斯于2010年共同创立了DeepMind，四年后，据当时报道，谷歌以6.5亿美元收购了该研究实验室。他的联合创始人穆斯塔法·苏莱曼目前是微软AI部门的主管。谷歌正在与其他主要AI开发商竞争客户，包括微软、OpenAI、Anthropic和Meta，以及中国的DeepSeek和Moonshot。

该行业还在追逐一个理论里程碑，即高级通用智能（AGI），这是AI软件达到人类思维能力的一个点。“我一生都在致力于AGI，现在，像你们中的许多人一样，我觉得它近在咫尺，”哈萨比斯在周三的博客文章中写道。“在这种背景下，我决定现在是时候将我在（谷歌DeepMind）的日常运营职责交接出去，以便我有时间和空间专注于大局，并帮助影响未来，”哈萨比斯继续说道。观察者一直在等待谷歌宣布其AI模型更强大的版本，称为Gemini 3.5 Pro，该模型原定于6月发布，但似乎已被推迟。其股价周三下午收盘下跌4%。
